Monday.subject: English
Monday.title: Blend and segment words
activities: Sound and blend these words: sat, map, dog, sun and pin.
Use counters for each sound in cat, sit, mop, run and tap. Push the counters together and say the whole word.
Adult says: map, dog, sun, pin and cat. Child stretches each word and writes the sounds they hear.
challenges: Read these words without counters: stop, frog and clap.
Choose one word and write a short sentence using it.

Tuesday.subject: Mathematics
Tuesday.title: Addition and subtraction within 10
activities: Use toy cars or Lego to solve: 5 + 2, 6 - 2, 4 + 4 and 9 - 3.
challenges: Mia has 4 blocks and gets 3 more. How many blocks does she have altogether?
There are 9 birds. 4 fly away. How many birds remain?

Wednesday.subject: English
Wednesday.title: Read and write a simple sentence
activities: Read: The dog can sit on the mat. Then write a new sentence about a cat.
Put these words in the correct order: cat / the / sat / mat / on / the.
Look at a favourite toy and write one sentence about it. Check for a capital letter, spaces and a full stop.
challenges: Write two connected sentences about the same picture or toy.
Add one describing word to your sentence, for example big, red, soft or fast.

Thursday.subject: Mathematics
Thursday.title: Repeating patterns
activities: Continue this AB pattern: red, blue, red, blue, red, __, __.
Continue this AAB pattern: star, star, triangle, star, star, triangle, __, __, __.
Use Lego, blocks, spoons or other household objects to make an ABC repeating pattern.
challenges: Create your own repeating pattern and explain which part repeats.
Find and fix the mistake in this pattern: red, blue, red, blue, blue, red, blue.

Friday.subject: Science
Friday.title: Material detectives
activities: Find one plastic object, one metal object and one paper object. Describe each using words such as smooth, rough, hard, soft, bendy or stiff.
Choose three safe household objects and group them by the material they are made from.
Compare a spoon and a paper towel. Talk about how their materials are different.
challenges: Why would ordinary paper be a poor material for making a drinking cup?
Choose a useful material for a raincoat and explain why you chose it.

reasoning.question: In the pattern red, blue, red, blue, what two colours repeat?

science.question: Which is usually harder: a metal spoon or a paper towel?

materials.question: Is a metal spoon usually hard or soft?
